shareCommentary.text:
I swept every company job board reachable through the public APIs of Greenhouse, Ashby and Lever — 9,152 boards, 285,289 open postings — to ask one question: who just started hiring?

Not who has jobs open. Who is hiring faster than they were a month ago.

Measured today, nothing modelled:

• 2,760 companies ramping — opening roles above their own prior rate
• 1,138 boards that did not exist 60 days ago
• 3,220 steady, 2,031 quiet
• 0 undated postings — all three vendors stamp every posting with a usable date, which is the only reason any of this is computable

Technology demand across everything opened in the last 90 days:
Python 19,731 · AWS 12,055 · Salesforce 9,874 · LLM 9,237 · Kubernetes 6,872

Two things I would want to know if I were reading someone else's version of this.

The sweep is partial, and I would rather say so than round it off. Greenhouse (5,506 boards) and Ashby (3,153) are complete. Lever reached 493 of 1,538 — Lever publishes Crawl-delay: 1 in its robots.txt, and 1,538 boards at one request per second is 26 minutes. Ignoring that would have made the number complete and destroyed the only claim here a scraper cannot make: that every figure comes from a vendor's own public API, fetched the way the vendor asked.

And I cut two things that were true but useless. "122 executive seats open" — seniority inferred from job titles does not survive aggregation once a single staffing firm posts 2,334 roles. Department labels like "Acacia Division (ACD) - 1047" are internal cost codes: accurate from the API, noise to a human. Both are still in the download. Neither belongs in a headline.

Full register, free, no signup — CSV and JSON alongside it, method and code public:
https://veresk06.github.io/open-ats-feed/ramp.html
